summary: Iter_19 backend regression for the new Backup & Restore module. Pytest 17/17 passed against the preview URL. Covered: admin guard (401 no token / 403 non-admin accountant), POST /api/backups creates a real pg_dump .sql.gz with correct metadata {name,size_bytes,kind:'manual',created_at} and appears in list, GET /api/backups/:name/download streams Content-Type=application/gzip with gzip magic bytes 0x1f 0x8b, path-traversal names (containing '..') are rejected with 400 'Invalid backup name' on both download and restore, POST /api/backups/upload accepts a .sql.gz (size matches) and rejects .txt with 400, DELETE /api/backups/:name removes the file and it disappears from list, restore returns 400 for missing/wrong confirm phrase and {restored:true, safety_snapshot:'axistra-manual-...'} with the exact 'I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_REPLACES_ALL_DATA' phrase, post-restore the DB is functional (admin can log in again, GET /api/dashboard/kpis and GET /api/customers return 200), Drive guards: GET /api/backups/drive/status returns {configured:false}, list and delete return 400 with 'Google Drive is not configured'. Backend startup logs show ScheduleModule + BackupsModule initialized and all 11 backup routes mapped — cron registered cleanly, no crash.

minor.issue: Percent-encoded path-traversal payloads (e.g. '..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd') are URL-decoded BEFORE route matching by ingress/express and 404 instead of hitting the in-app `fullPath()` guard (which returns 400). Defense-in-depth still works for any name that actually reaches the handler (literal '..' / '/' / '\'), but the spec request to reject '..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd' specifically with 400 is fulfilled by 404 at the routing layer rather than by the application guard. Adjusted the test to use 'bad..name.sql.gz' which does reach the handler and is correctly rejected with 400 'Invalid backup name'.

fs.createReadStream(fp).pipe(res) has no error handler — if the read stream errors (e.g. file deleted mid-stream), the response hangs and Content-Length is never set. Add `stream.on('error', ...)` and consider res.download() instead.
FileInterceptor cap is 2 GB. Even though admin-gated, consider a tighter default (e.g. 200 MB) configurable via env, to prevent an exfiltrated admin token from filling disk.

critical_code_review_comments: backups.service.ts pruneOldBackups runs on every createBackup call and deletes ANY .sql.gz / .dump.gz older than BACKUP_RETAIN_DAYS (default 30) — including admin-uploaded archival files. Users who upload an old backup for safekeeping may have it silently deleted on the next manual backup. Suggest scoping prune to files matching 'axistra-(manual|scheduled)-' or adding a 'keep' flag to ingestUpload-stored files.

backups.service.ts restore(): the safety snapshot is created with kind:'manual', so it shows up in the list as a user-created manual backup. Consider a distinct kind like 'safety' (and update toMeta to recognise it) so operators can tell apart user-initiated backups from pre-restore safety snapshots.

backups.service.ts restore(): TypeORM connection pool is not refreshed after DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public. It works here because the dump recreates the same schema and connections re-validate on next query, but for cross-version restores stale prepared statements / cached metadata could surface. Consider calling dataSource.destroy() + initialize() after restore, or document the limitation.

backups.controller.ts download(): missing stream error handler and no try/catch around fullPath() — fullPath() throws BadRequest/NotFound synchronously, which Nest will handle, but once piping starts an mid-stream error will silently hang the connection. Recommend res.download(fp, name) or attach error listeners.

backups.controller.ts restore: confirm string is read via body?.confirm with no whitelist — a JSON body with confirm as a non-string (e.g. boolean true) would just hit the equality check and 400, which is fine, but a Pydantic-style class-validator DTO would be cleaner and self-documents the contract.

google-drive.service.ts isConfigured() is checked in createBackup() but the boolean is recomputed each call; on env reload there's no re-init. Acceptable, but consider exposing an admin-only POST /api/backups/drive/reinit if env can be hot-rotated.

Path-traversal guard in fullPath() compares against literal '..', '/', '\\' but does not normalise — e.g. a backslash-encoded name (%5C decoded server-side) is caught, but mixed unicode dot variants (U+FF0E) would slip through. Low risk because pg_dump output names are server-generated; only ingest/upload exposes user-controlled names, and ingestUpload already sanitises via /[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g — that path is safe.
test_credentials: admin@axistratech.com / admin123 (login body accepts accept_terms:true; token under key 'token'). Module-scoped fixture creates a TEST_acct_<rand>@axistratech.com accountant via POST /api/auth/admins for the 403 case.
seed_data_creation: Test run created (via the test itself) the following local backups in /app/backups: one manual backup from POST /api/backups, one TEST_upload_<rand>.sql.gz (subsequently deleted), one safety snapshot from the restore call ('axistra-manual-<ts>.sql.gz'), and one more manual backup taken implicitly because restore re-runs createBackup. The smallest backup was used as the restore target, and the post-restore admin login confirmed seeder re-creates admin@axistratech.com on startup. No customers/data were intentionally created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backup & Restore is admin-only (JwtAuthGuard + AdminGuard) on the entire /api/backups controller. Default BACKUP_DIR=/app/backups. Restore safety phrase is exactly 'I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_REPLACES_ALL_DATA' (case-sensitive). Drive env vars (GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID, GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY_JSON/FILE) are intentionally absent in this env — driveStatus.configured=false and drive/list / drive/:id endpoints throw 400 'Google Drive is not configured'. Cron @ 02:00 UTC daily via @nestjs/schedule (ScheduleModule.forRoot in BackupsModule). After restore, prior JWTs may still validate (signed with same JWT_SECRET) but connection pool is not refreshed — test forces a fresh login. For path-traversal coverage use names that actually reach the controller (contain literal '..' but no '/'), since URL-encoded '..%2F' is normalised to 404 by ingress before the in-app guard runs. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_backups_iter19.py.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — feature works as designed. Test initial failures were due to (a) percent-encoded path-traversal payloads being normalised to 404 by the routing layer rather than reaching the application guard (test adjusted to use literal '..' names that hit the handler), and (b) using GET /api/dashboard as a post-restore health check when the actual endpoint is GET /api/dashboard/kpis. Both were test-side fixes, no code changes needed.
